column1: # THE BY-NAME CLAIM CENSUS -- clause 3 of S5's exit gate, built by slice S6 2026-08-27.
# WHAT IT IS FOR, in the exit gate's own words: "so a mechanism that quietly loses its
# claim in translation is visible as a MISSING ROW rather than as a smaller number."
# The Python biosphere suite is deleted by this slice's successor; this file is the record
# of what each of its claims became, one row per test FUNCTION, and it outlives its input.
# HOW IT WAS BUILT -- extracted, not read. Both rosters come from disk (455 `def test_*`
# across S5's twenty files; every `#[test] fn` AND every `gate <name> {` in the eleven
# biosphere surfaces). Dispositions come, in priority order, from: an S6 override list
# (evidence `S6`, and only where this slice measurably falsified an earlier one); the
# REFERENCE'S OWN docstrings, where a Rust test names the Python test it mirrors (evidence
# `docstring`); the plan's authored disposition tables (evidence: the section that wrote
# them); and rules written by S6 for the remainder (evidence `S6`). A Python test matched
# by none of the four is a hard error in the generator, which is what makes this an
# expansion rather than a transcription -- a coverage table built by READING cannot see
# its own omissions, and this repo has been bitten by that twice.
# THE DENOMINATOR, decided once and stated here. `science.rs`, `flows.rs`, `params.rs` and
# `system.rs` are the four surfaces S5 landed on: every test in them must be CLAIMED, by a
# `P` row that names it or by an `A` row that declares it. The other seven surfaces are
# claimable but not required, because they descend from Python files outside S5's twenty.
# WHAT AN `A` ROW MEANS: a Rust test no Python claim maps to. `outside-the-20` is derived
# from the test's own doc block, or from the plan's port-coverage table where a whole
# surface descends from one file. `no-ancestor-named` is a claim the reference makes that
# the Python biosphere suite never made -- additional coverage, not a translation.
# ⚠ THIS FILE IS A FORCING FUNCTION AND THAT COSTS SOMETHING. `claim_census.rs` pins the
# row counts and the `open`+`S6` count as literals, so a new biosphere test reddens the
# census until it is declared here. That is the point, not friction to be removed: the
#   ported          a Rust test carries the claim
#   owned           pre-existing Rust coverage, from the Phase-7 port or an earlier slice
#   folded          subsumed by a different and usually stronger mechanism
#   compiler        enforced by the type system or by `include_str!`, harder than a test
#   engine          enforced by the engine itself (`assert_conserved` runs every step)
#   boundary        owned one layer down, at the param-file boundary crate: its schema
#                   check, its exact-string unit guard, its required `{value, unit, source}`
#   decided-out     no successor, by a RECORDED port decision (science.rs's module header)
#   no-subject      the subject was never built here: design records, refused branches,
#                   and constructions that exist only inside the Python test file
#   retired-subject the subject existed in the reference and was DELETED
#   python-only     the subject is the Python tree itself; it dies with it
#   open            no successor and no decision -- a gap, carried forward
